hints: Start with the sample proportion $\hat{p} = \dfrac{1602}{2000}$. The variance of a sample proportion is $\dfrac{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})}{n}$ with $n = 2000$; set that up.
A confidence interval has the form $\hat{p} \pm z \times \sqrt{\dfrac{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})}{n}}$. The square root of the variance you just set up is the standard error, so take it.
For a 95% interval, the middle 95% is covered, so 2.5% sits in each tail. Find the $z$ value that leaves 2.5% in the upper tail (normal table or inverse normal on your calculator).
Work out $\hat{p} - z \times (\text{standard error})$ and $\hat{p} + z \times (\text{standard error})$, then write the answer as an interval, "... to ...", correct to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
**What we are doing**

We have one sample of 2000 adults. We want a range of values that is likely to contain the true proportion of all adults who own a smartphone. That range is called a **confidence interval**. A 95% confidence interval means we use the middle 95% of a normal distribution.

The method: take the sample proportion, then go a bit below and a bit above it. How far we go depends on the standard error and on a $z$ value.

**Find the sample proportion**

$\hat{p}$ (say "p-hat") means the proportion in our sample that own a smartphone. 1602 out of 2000 did.

$$\hat{p} = \frac{1602}{2000} = 0.801$$

Quick check: 1602 is a bit over 80% of 2000 (80% of 2000 is 1600), so 0.801 makes sense.

**Work out the variance of the sample proportion (first M1)**

For a proportion, the variance is $\dfrac{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})}{n}$, where $n = 2000$ is the sample size. First the $(1-\hat{p})$ part:

$$1 - 0.801 = 0.199$$

Now multiply the two proportions:

$$0.801 \times 0.199 = 0.159399$$

Then divide by $n = 2000$:

$$\frac{0.159399}{2000} = 0.0000796995 \approx 0.0000797$$

This earns the first M1. Keep the unrounded number on your calculator for later.

**Take the square root to get the standard error**

The variance is in squared units. The **standard error** is its square root:

$$\sqrt{0.0000796995} = 0.0089275\ldots$$

Calculator: type $\sqrt{(0.801 \times 0.199 \div 2000)}$ and press equals.

**Choose the $z$ value (B1)**

For a 95% confidence interval, 95% of the normal curve is in the middle. That leaves 5% in the two tails, so 2.5% in each tail. The $z$ value with 2.5% above it is the one where $\Phi(z) = 0.975$.

Normal table, or inverse normal on your calculator with area 0.975:

$$z = 1.96$$

This earns the B1. It is a value worth remembering: $1.96$ is the standard 95% two-sided value.

**Write the interval (second M1 and A1)**

The interval is $\hat{p} \pm z \times (\text{standard error})$. First the "give or take" amount:

$$1.96 \times 0.0089275 = 0.017498\ldots$$

Now subtract and add it to $0.801$:

$$\text{lower} = 0.801 - 0.017498 = 0.783502$$

$$\text{upper} = 0.801 + 0.017498 = 0.818498$$

Round each to 3 significant figures: $0.783502 \to 0.784$ and $0.818498 \to 0.818$ (the digit after is 5 or more for the first, under 5 for the second). The M1 is for the form $\hat{p} \pm z \times \text{standard error}$ and the A1 is for the final interval.

Common slip: giving only the half-width $0.0175$, or writing $0.801 \pm 0.0175$ and stopping. The mark scheme requires a proper interval, from one value to another.

**Final answer**

An approximate 95% confidence interval for the proportion of adults who own a smartphone is

$$0.784 \text{ to } 0.818 \quad (3\text{ sf})$$

(The mark scheme also allows $0.783$ to $0.819$.)
